triage: C-with-named-side-effect (implementation landed, numerics identical, whole-implementation slower)

identity.cpu_check: CPU_PLAN_OK 152 rows, 232 passes, 502 buffers; no Vulkan loaded

layer1_source_intent: Pack 4 token8 tiles x 2 channel groups per workgroup instead of 2 tiles x 4 groups, so a workgroup keeps half as many distinct weight slabs resident (512 KiB -> 256 KiB) while replaying each slab from 2 instead of 1 workgroup per y-slice. No arithmetic, no K order, no SLM, no scratch change.

layer2_native.identification: ISA file name changes only for the F08 kernel (CS_asm3b9ac75d... -> CS_asm3de9ecb0...); the other 39 kernels are byte-identical across the two arms
observed_changes: shl 4 -> shl 5 on the token index (x16 -> x32)
shl 2 -> shl 1 on the group index (x4 -> x2)
+1 instruction (address setup), first DPAS 2 instructions later
hash constants at the closing mov (code identity, not semantics)
unchanged: same workgroup memory (2048 B, declared in SPV)
layer2_native.verdict: IMPLEMENTED (A-class excluded): the integer index change is present in ISA and nothing else moved

layer3_numeric_resources.resources_stage: both arms COMPLETED with gold frame (GpuTime single hardware pass, not additive)

layer4_timing.design: one batch, 6 alternating process pairs (base/cand), 30 samples per arm per pair, warm1 reps30 feedback; 360 samples, all retained, no trimming, no rerun

attribution.claimed: none beyond the direction of the trade
named_side_effects_present: per-workgroup deduplicated input footprint 16 KiB -> 32 KiB (2x)
4 subgroups of one group slab run concurrently inside a workgroup (phase drift can thrash the same lines)
dispatch geometry y 2 -> 4 changes workgroup launch order and therefore which kernels share a core wave
attribution.cannot_split: whether the regression comes from the input-footprint doubling, from the same-slab phase drift, or from the changed dispatch order cannot be separated with the available tools

decision: NOT ADOPTED. Baseline pointer unchanged. The direction 'group weights by workgroup for cache locality' is not refuted: this candidate traded 2x weight-slab reuse for 2x input footprint in the same change, and that trade lost 0.18 ms on this shape.

next_discriminating_experiment.experiment: same workgroup content (4 tiles x 2 groups) with the dispatch transposed to grid (4,33) instead of (33,4): identical footprints, identical ISA arithmetic, only the launch order changes
next_discriminating_experiment.decision_rule: if (4,33) recovers the 0.18 ms, the regression is dispatch order, not footprint; if it stays slow, the input-footprint/staleness axis is the cause
